rationales: Genus is a taxonomic rank above species.
Order is a higher taxonomic rank than species.
Species is the basic unit of classification.
Class is a higher taxonomic rank than species.
Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane, not general movement against a concentration gradient.
Active transport moves molecules from lower to higher concentration using energy.
Passive transport does not require energy and generally moves substances down their concentration gradient.
Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from higher to lower concentration.
Prophase is a stage of cell division, not the phase with the cell’s highest overall metabolic activity.
Metaphase is a stage of cell division when chromosomes align.
Interphase is when the cell grows and carries out most of its metabolic activities.
Anaphase is a stage of cell division when sister chromatids separate.
Lipase does not digest starch; amylase does.
Lipase does not digest proteins; proteases do.
Lipase does not act on vitamins as its substrate.
Lipase breaks down lipids.
A habitat is the place where an organism lives, not a group of organisms.
The biosphere includes all regions of Earth where life exists.
A community consists of populations of different species living together.
A population is members of the same species living in the same place at the same time.
Physiology studies the functions of organisms and their parts.
Morphology studies the form and structure of organisms.
Histology is the microscopic study of tissues.
Ecology studies relationships between organisms and their environment.
Plasmodium is the microorganism that causes malaria.
Entamoeba is associated with amoebic dysentery, not malaria.
Paramecium is a ciliate and does not cause malaria.
E. coli is a bacterium and does not cause malaria.
Related genera are grouped into a family.
A phylum is a higher rank than family.
A class is a higher rank than family.
An order is a higher rank than family.
Peroxisomes carry out oxidative reactions, not protein synthesis.
Lysosomes digest cellular materials and do not synthesize proteins.
Vacuoles mainly store substances and do not synthesize proteins.
Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.
Plastids perform functions such as photosynthesis and storage, not most cellular energy production.
Mitochondria are the major sites of cellular energy production.
Ribosomes synthesize proteins.
Golgi bodies modify, sort, and package cellular products.
Sea stars can regenerate lost parts through cell division, including mitosis.
Horses do not regenerate lost limbs through mitosis.
Mosquitoes do not regenerate lost body parts in this way.
Frogs do not regenerate lost parts in the manner described.
Formic acid is not a vitamin that acts as a coenzyme.
Nucleic acid is not a vitamin.
An amino acid is a building block of proteins, not a vitamin.
Folic acid is a vitamin that functions as a coenzyme precursor.
Stomata cover about 1–2% of the leaf surface.
The commonly stated coverage is not as high as 1–5%.
Stomata do not cover as much as 5–10% of the leaf surface.
The commonly stated coverage is lower than 2–8%.
Zinc is a micronutrient but is not the one identified here as required in nitrogen metabolism.
Iron has important roles in plants, but nickel is specifically associated with nitrogen metabolism.
Chlorine is a micronutrient involved in functions such as photosynthesis and osmotic balance.
Nickel is required for nitrogen metabolism, including the functioning of urease.
One gram of protein provides about 4 kilocalories, not 8.
One gram of protein provides about 4 kilocalories, not 6.
One gram of protein provides about 4 kilocalories.
One gram of protein provides about 4 kilocalories, not 2.
